A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Informed Correctors for Discrete Diffusion Models. Their complete 22-page contents, including appendices A–D, are readable, and text extraction plus visual inspection supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 5.1–5.3 and Appendix D report original synthetic Markov-chain simulations, Text8 experiments, and ImageNet generation results.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results and adds numerical results comparing confidence scores in Appendix D.3.4.

M1.justification: Appendix B and Algorithm 1 remove the corrector-entry threshold t_c = 0.9 and the instruction to skip correction when t > t_c. The described sampler consequently permits correction after every predictor step. The architecture, training objectives, and confidence-score formulas remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic Markov-chain task, Text8 character modeling, and class-conditional ImageNet 256x256 generation. The new confidence-score ablation stays within existing coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding benchmark comparisons retain their comparator sets, including MD4, uninformed correctors, ReMDM, MaskGIT, DPC, and VQ-Diffusion. The newly cited LLaDA is discussed but not evaluated; Table 4 ablates existing confidence options.

E3.justification: The reported sampling procedure removes the correction-time restriction in Appendix B. Table 4 also adds a confidence-choice comparison for two existing model configurations. These changes do not establish that the retained benchmark experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix D.3.4 and Table 4 quantify the effect of log-likelihood versus margin confidence for HollowDiff and MD4 with informed correction. v4 describes both options and qualitatively favors margin confidence, but lacks this numerical ablation. Existing analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over five random seeds for the synthetic experiment. The new confidence ablation supplies point FID values without introducing run counts, uncertainty estimates, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Table 4 newly reports log-likelihood-confidence FIDs of 6.45 for HollowDiff and 5.85 for MD4 with informed correction. Its margin-confidence values, 6.26 and 5.78, already appear in v4. Existing table values, plotted results, and generated examples are retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Proposition 3.3.1, and derivations in Appendices A–C remain unchanged. The added related-work discussion about first-order marginal preservation supplies an interpretation rather than a new formal derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same central contributions and claims about informed correction, hollow transformers, complementary training signals, and improved sampling quality.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 now explicitly qualifies hybrid-model gains by its 400M parameters versus 230M for individual models and explains excessive parallel updates through ignored dependencies and conflicting corrections. Section 4 adds a contrast between marginal-preserving correction and potentially biased confidence-ordered remasking.

D1.justification: v5 deletes the explicit synthetic-experiment settings S = 4, D = 128, p = 0.9, and the cosine masking schedule from Section 5.1 without restoring them in Appendix D. Hardware, real-data training recipes, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4 adds a citation to LLaDA and distinguishes its remasking heuristics from informed Gibbs selection. The remaining cited works are retained; subsequent reference-number changes do not represent new research coverage.

P1.justification: v5 makes localized revisions to related work and experimental interpretation, shortens the synthetic-experiment description, adds an ablation subsection and cross-references, and replaces the preprint footer with NeurIPS 2025 conference text. The overall narrative structure remains.

P2.justification: v5 adds Table 4, expands Figure 4’s caption, and shortens Algorithm 1. Figure 5 and Table 3 move within the appendix as text reflows. Existing plots and generated-image panels are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Table 4 adds useful evidence for the confidence choice, and Section 5.3 more clearly acknowledges the hybrid model’s larger parameter count. However, v5 removes synthetic-experiment reproducibility settings and changes correction timing without explaining its relationship to retained results. These evidence gains and documentation losses leave the net effect on overall quality uncertain.
